thread:
maya: Heads-up: docs PR #514 needs a runtime check. I added an SDK example that sets request.priority=5 and a note that "higher numeric priority is preferred". CI preview passed but we need to confirm server-side behavior and default precedence before merging.
alan: quick note: runtime interprets priority as relative integer; larger = higher. But there's also deployment.routingPolicy.minPriority that can clamp or reject requests. We should be explicit about that in the docs.
maya: snippet I added:

```
from redwood import Client
c = Client()
r = c.generate("Hello", route="critical", request_options={"priority": 5})
```

maya: PR text currently: "Set request priority to prefer this work during congestion." Should we change wording?
rachel: hold merge until we clarify precedence and defaults. Also mention that Hosted default routing allows per-request priority, Dedicated/Private may enforce deployment-level limits.
alan: right. Suggest wording: "Requests may set a numeric priority (larger = higher). The router honors request priority unless the deployment's routing policy enforces a min/max or clamping behavior."
maya: good. Any special behavior on negative or 0 values? I used 0 in some examples elsewhere.
alan: runtime treats missing priority as 0. Negative values are allowed but lower than 0 and deprioritized; however deployments can set a minPriority of 0 to reject negatives. I'll add a parenthetical about clamping.
ci-bot: preview ready for PR #514  https://preview.docs.redwood.ai/pr/514 (status: success)
maya: thanks. @docs-bot add label "merge-on-config-clarity" please.
docs-bot: label "merge-on-config-clarity" added by docs-bot.
rachel: please update PR with the new sentence, note default=0, and a short table of precedence: 1) deployment.routingPolicy.min/maxPriority 2) request.request_options.priority 3) route-level defaults. Keep it short.
maya: updated PR with wording, default note, and tiny precedence list. PTAL.
alan: LGTM from runtime side, added comment about clamping and negative values.
rachel: approved, merging in the midday window. Add a migration note for Dedicated customers who had relied on negative priorities.
maya: thanks all, merging now. :shipit:
